description: Code Cartel is a team of passionate, innovative and ambitious young developers interested in artificial intelligence, technology, agriculture and solving real-world challenges. We aim to use creativity, teamwork, coding and NASA Earth observation data to develop innovative solutions that can make a meaningful impact on communities and the agricultural sector. We are enthusiastic individuals with skills in Python, AI/ML, data science, satellite imagery, GIS, agriculture, research and UI/UX design
summary: AquaRoot is an agricultural technology concept developed by Code Cartel to help farmers address challenges such as unpredictable rainfall, water shortages, changing temperatures and declining soil health. It combines NASA satellite data with underground soil sensors to monitor environmental conditions and support smarter irrigation decisions, helping farmers determine when watering is actually necessary. Artificial Intelligence was used as an assisting tool during development to support research, explore solutions and refine the system's decision-making approach, while the team developed the concept and its technical direction. Beyond irrigation, AquaRoot aims to provide crop-rotation recommendations to help farmers maintain soil health, manage nutrients and adapt to changing seasons. Its importance lies in its potential to make agricultural technology more affordable and accessible, reduce water wastage and promote sustainable farming, especially for smallholder farmers who lack access to expensive agricultural resources.
details: # Project Description: AquaRoot – The Root That Thinks AquaRoot is an AI-powered agricultural intelligence project created by Code Cartel to help farmers make data-driven decisions. The project uses intelligence and environmental data to assess agricultural conditions and provide useful insights for both crop production and livestock management. It works by collecting and analyzing observations, including NASA POWER satellite-derived data to identify conditions that may affect farming. The system processes this information to produce assessments that can help farmers understand agricultural risks and make more informed decisions. Benefits: AquaRoot aims to improve decision-making support early identification of environmental risks reduce potential farming losses and make useful agricultural information more accessible. It also has the potential to help farmers who may not have access to agricultural monitoring technologies. Intended impact: Our goal is to contribute to more sustainable agriculture, particularly in South Africa, where farmers face challenges such as changing weather conditions, water shortages and unpredictable environmental patterns. We want to support food security protect resources and help strengthen farming communities. Tools and technologies: We developed the project using Python as the programming language. Our development tools and technologies included Streamlit for the user interface Pandas for data processing SQLite for data storage and NASA POWER API for data. We also used intelligence and machine-learning concepts to support agricultural analysis and interpretation. Innovation: What makes AquaRoot creative is its combination of space-based data, artificial intelligence and agricultural applications in one platform. Of presenting farmers with raw environmental data it aims to transform observations into understandable agricultural insights. Its focus on both livestock and crops also makes it adaptable, to farming needs. Factors considered: Our team considered the accessibility of technology the challenges faced by South African farmers, environmental sustainability, data reliability, affordability and the practical needs of farming communities. We also considered the importance of developing a system that can grow through testing, training and farmer feedback.
